title: Persist per-user categories in backend and load them under Favorites on login

requirements.text: Ensure categories are persisted per authenticated user in the backend and are returned for that same user after logging out and logging back in.

quotes: Maybe make a create category below the "Favorites" - but every user has to make their own categories. But once made they should always show unless deleted.

acceptanceCriteria: When a signed-in user creates categories, logs out, and logs back in, calling the backend categories list returns the previously created categories for that user.
Categories created by User A do not appear for User B.
Backend rejects category CRUD calls from anonymous callers consistently (no silent failures).

requirements.text: Fix backend category CRUD semantics so that category identity used by the frontend (category name strings) matches backend storage and prompt detaching/renaming logic end-to-end.

quotes: But once made they should always show unless deleted.

acceptanceCriteria: Renaming a category updates the stored category entry and updates every prompt that references the old category name so it references the new category name.
Deleting a category detaches it from all prompts by removing that category name from each prompt’s categories array, keeps the prompts, and removes the category from backend storage.
After rename/delete, subsequent getAllCategories returns the updated category name list with no stale entries.

requirements.text: Persist backend state across canister upgrades for per-user prompts and categories so that user-created categories are not lost after deployment upgrades.

quotes: But once made they should always show unless deleted.

acceptanceCriteria: After a canister upgrade, existing users’ prompts and categories are still present.
If a migration is needed for existing stored data, it runs conditionally and does not corrupt user data.

requirements.text: On successful login, automatically load categories from the backend and render them immediately below the "Favorites" control in the category UI.

quotes: Works great but when I log in to the app the categories are not there. I want the categories that have been created to always show below "Favorites"
Immediately on login, if they have been created already.

acceptanceCriteria: After login completes and backend connectivity succeeds, the UI shows the user’s categories under the Favorites control without requiring a manual refresh.
If the backend returns categories, the categories list in the UI matches the backend list (including after a full page reload).
If backend connectivity fails, the UI displays an error state and does not misleadingly show an empty categories list as if no categories exist.

requirements.text: Add an always-available "Create category" entry directly below the "Favorites" control, and ensure creating a category persists it to the backend for the current user.

quotes: Maybe make a create category below the "Favorites"

acceptanceCriteria: The category UI includes a clear create-category control placed directly below Favorites.
Creating a category updates the UI immediately and persists the new category to the backend; after logout/login it still appears.
Attempting to create a duplicate category (case-insensitive) is prevented with a user-facing message in English.

requirements.text: Ensure all category mutations from the UI (create, rename, delete) call the backend-backed sync actions so the backend remains the source of truth after login.

quotes: But once made they should always show unless deleted.

acceptanceCriteria: Create/rename/delete category actions from the category UI trigger backend calls and reflect success/failure to the user in English.
After any category mutation, the categories shown below Favorites remain consistent with the backend response (including after refreshFromBackend).

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo.
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or the immutable hook paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT; compose them instead.
nonGoals: Third-party authentication providers other than Internet Identity.
Real-time syncing between multiple sessions/devices beyond loading on login and explicit refresh.
